changes.title: Label preview drafts and promote the newest stable release
changes.body:
## Summary

Recovery drafts used commit SHAs as titles, and the workflow explicitly disabled Latest for every stable release.

| When | GitHub release update |
| --- | --- |
| A PR merges | Name the recovery draft with the PR number and title. |
| npm verifies a preview | Rename the same draft with the npm version and PR number, and mark it Pre-release. |
| A stable release publishes | Set Latest if this is the highest published stable version. Older maintenance releases preserve the badge. |

## Evidence

The release-command test reproduced the missing preview label. It now verifies that a retry preserves the draft, its original tag, and its assets without creating a second entry. Stable release tests cover promotion and recovery after a newer version has shipped. Typechecking and all 374 tests passed.

## Merge Danger

The change is reversible and affects GitHub release metadata. Reverting restores the previous behavior for future runs. Maintainers can edit titles and labels already applied.
changes.head: jwood/github-release-labels
changes.author: dumptruckman

changes.title: Record the analyzer version in JSON reports and define v1 scoring compatibility
changes.body:
## Summary

An old JSON report gives you no way to tell which version of ouch4ts generated it. Current and comparison reports now include `analyzerVersion` on disk and in JSON stdout, even when a filter matches nothing.

```json
{ "analyzerVersion": "0.1.3", "entries": [], "files": [] }
```

The v1 compatibility policy covers the CLI, typed API, and saved report formats. Changing an existing scoring rule requires a major release. A patch can fix a calculation to match a published rule. Its release notes identify which scores can change.

## Evidence

- The current and comparison report tests failed on the missing field before the change. Both now check the saved file and filtered stdout against the package version.
- A comparison test changes the installed analyzer version and reuses both cached revisions. The new report records the running version.
- Typecheck and all 374 tests passed after rebasing onto `main`.

## Merge danger

Merging with `release:major` publishes an npm preview and prepares the rolling release PR for `1.0.0`. Merging that separate PR publishes the stable package.
changes.head: jwood/v1-compatibility
changes.author: dumptruckman
